title: Edgar Hayes and the hundred-dollar bill in San Francisco
summary: With Edgar Hayes's Riverside-era group, a woman tipped Bunn a hundred dollars on the bandstand, Hayes tried to take it and Bunn hit him, then Hayes cut his finger at his door.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: What do you think you'd be doing now, if you were working?
You mean you'd like to get your own group again --
-- or play with Edgar Hayes again, or something like that?
No, I wouldn't want to be with no Edgar.
What was it like -- what kind of -- what were you doing with him? That was like Riverside?
Yeah. In -- what's that town up here? Where you went.
Him and I had a fight up there. He got jealous of me.
What is he now, is he a piano player?

A girl liked me and she come to the bandstand and we was playing. Give me a hundred dollar bill. She said, 'This is for you.' Edgar saw it and he tried to get it from me, and I pushed him away from me. So he stopped the band. Stopped the band. Intermission. So he called me to him, and I went up to him. 'Give me that money, Teddy.' I said, 'The girl give it to me.'
And she said, 'This is yours.' And I told

him. So he grabbed my hand and said, "Give me the money." And I told him no and I hit him. What the hell is he grabbing me for, hitting me in front of all these people. I popped him and I knocked the shit out of him.
It was a hundred dollar bill, man.
Shit, I wasn't going to give that up. For what? She gave it to me. She'd been watching me all night long. Right in Frisco.
Uh-huh. Now, why do you think she'd do a thing like that?

God knows. I didn't care as long as I had it. Shoot, man, And I gave a party at my room that night, and he come in there and knocked on the door, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, he liked to tore the door down. And when I opened it he rushed in and cut me on the finger. He had a little knife, and he cut me on the finger. When I opened the door. And I knocked the shit out of him. And he was going around with a white thing on his head where I knocked the shit out of him. He was going around, up and down. Oh, boy. And I shut my door and locked it.
Oh, boy. It's get crazy, doesn't it, sometimes.
For what? What did he do that for?

Give him the money. Now, the girl saw him out there, and if she had wanted him to have it she would have said, 'Mr. Hayes, this is for you,' you know? Split it with the band. But no, he come taking it away from me, after she give it to me. Wouldn't wait for me to say, 'Here, Edgar, here's something that we got a tip.' What the hell is he going to take it from me for? So I popped him. And he was going around with this thing on his head, man, all up and down, and the band was -- the rest of the guys in the band was laughing. Boy, they was laughing, because they said Edgar didn't have no business doing that. He didn't. He was drinking, you know. Right up there in San Francisco, at a club.
